title: Add "Private install health" dashboard (installer/upgrade controller + component readiness)
author: Sergio Costa
release_notes: Private min pack: adds Install Health dashboard to baseline bundle (installer/upgrade controller and component readiness panels).
body: Context: Private installs have repeatedly stalled during upgrades or initial provisioning with little visibility beyond kubectl/helm output (see INT-1184 + recent staging drill notes). This PR adds a baseline "Private install health" Grafana dashboard to the min pack so on-call/operators can quickly answer: (1) is the installer/upgrade controller reconciling? (2) what component is not ready? (3) did a recent rollout correlate with readiness/latency regressions? What’s included: - New dashboard: "Private / Install Health" in the standard Private folder. - Panels: Installer reconcile success + latency (p50/p95), reconcile error rate and last error, current upgrade phase/state, last successful reconcile timestamp, component readiness table (gateway/runtime/control plane/observability deps), pod restart rate by component, and "stuck rollout" indicators (deployment progressing but replicas unavailable). - Standard annotations: adds shared annotations query for installer upgrade start/finish events (where present) and deploy/version annotations (when the environment emits them). Implementation notes: - Dashboard uses the pack’s variable templates ($cluster, $namespace, $environment) and conforms to the naming/templating conventions introduced in PR #318. - Metrics used are intentionally low-cardinality. Component readiness panels rely on kube-state-metrics (kube_deployment_status_* / kube_pod_container_status_*). Installer-specific panels use redwood_installer_* and redwood_upgrade_controller_* metrics (added in redwood core + installer workstreams; dashboard degrades gracefully if those series are absent and shows a helpful "missing signals" note). - Added "Required metrics" doc block at top of the dashboard JSON to make support validation easier and align with the supported-signals checklist work (ENG-2852). Screenshots: (omitted here; see Grafana preview in CI artifact "dashboard-render" job). Follow-ups: - Once redwood-private-installer PR for the post-install validation command lands, we should wire its output to point operators to this dashboard by name (ENG-2852). - If we decide to emit explicit reconcile events as Loki logs, we can add a log-panel to show the last N reconcile failures (not in scope for min pack v1).
commits: dashboards(private): add Install Health dashboard skeleton + variables
dashboards(private): add installer reconcile panels + error panels
dashboards(private): add standard annotations + doc header
chore(ci): include install-health dashboard in validation render list
conversation: Allison Grant (requested changes): "This is the right dashboard, but please tighten the semantics: 1) make the readiness table use consistent component names (gateway/runtime/control-plane/installer/obs), 2) ensure none of the queries accidentally join on pod name in a way that explodes cardinality, 3) add a short 'How to read this dashboard' note at the top." Sergio Costa (author): "Good call. Updated the component mapping to a fixed label->display map, removed pod-level joins in favor of deployment-level readiness, and added a top text panel with a quick triage flow." Bruno Silva (requested changes): "The installer metrics are new; in older envs this dashboard will be blank. Can we show an explicit warning when redwood_installer_reconcile_total is missing?" Sergio Costa: "Added a 'Missing signals' stat panel with a query that flips when the series is absent for >10m, plus a link to the supported-signals checklist." Sean Gallagher (comment): "Please make sure the 'stuck rollout' panel doesn’t page people by implication. Dashboard-only is fine, but keep the language neutral (no 'CRITICAL')." Sergio Costa: "Adjusted titles/threshold coloring to be informational; no paging language." Marcus Lin (comment): "Confirm no secrets/URLs in dashboards and annotations; also ensure grafana links don’t include tokens." Sergio Costa: "Confirmed; no secrets, and links are relative dashboard links only." Fatima Noor (comment): "On-prem minimal footprint: kube-state-metrics is sometimes not installed by customer. Do we have a fallback?" Sergio Costa: "Dashboard shows component readiness section as 'requires kube-state-metrics'; the installer panels still work. We can revisit bundling kube-state-metrics guidance in the install guide." Approvals: Allison Grant approved; Bruno Silva approved; Sean Gallagher approved.
final_outcome: Merged to main; dashboard included in Private minimum pack bundle starting next pack cut.
